I am a retired professor of Education Technology. As head of the [Department of Interactive Media and Educational Technologies](https://www.donau-uni.ac.at/en/university/faculties/education-arts-architecture/departments/continuing-education-research-educational-technologies.html) at the [University for Continuing Education Krems (UWK)](https://www.donau-uni.ac.at/en) (Austria), I researched how to apply technology in settings of Life Long Learning. 

I had held positions as a professor at several universities in Austria and Germany (Klagenfurt, Münster, Innsbruck, Hagen) before I accepted the nomination to Krems. I published 25 books (10 monographs and 15 edited volumes) and [over 200 articles](https://portfolio.peter-baumgartner.net/publication/).

Today, I remain interested in technology-enhanced learning (TEL), now focusing on workflows and tools for Open Science research (e.g., [Obsidian](https://obsidian.md/ "A note-taking app as extensible knowledge base"), [Hypothes.is](https://web.hypothes.is/ "Annotate anything online"), [Zotero](https://www.zotero.org/)). These subjects are covered predominantly in my [German weblog "Gedankensplitter"](https://peter.baumgartner.name).

However, I have also developed a new interest in statistical data processing and data science. My focus is on investigating social inequality and the decline of democratic structures. I am learning to apply Bayesian statistics using [R](https://www.r-project.org/) to these (for me) new research subjects. But in this area, I am still a learner, not an expert.
